local_patches.reason: Upstream builds pipeline_matmul_f32 from the coopmat or fp16 shader family, whose FLOAT_TYPE is float16_t, so an F32 x F32 matmul runs on F16-rounded operands. Uta! Studio's audio graphs are F32 end to end and decode greedily, so that changes output. This rebuilds only that pipeline from the scalar _fp32 shaders. UTA_STUDIO_GGML_F32_MATMUL=promote restores the upstream pipeline for the callers that have measured the trade and accepted it; absent is exact.

GGML's cooperative-matrix flash attention is gated on a 16x16x16 shape, so on Intel Xe, which reports only 8x16x16 through VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix, attention always falls back to the scalar shader and never reaches the matrix engine. Attention is about two thirds of a separation pass. M is the MatBc tile constant in flash_attn_cm1.comp, so this adds an M=8 build of the same shader and selects it where that is the only shape the device has. It also makes that shader honour GGML_PREC_F32 in the PV accumulator, which upstream leaves in float16_t; without that the coopmat path moves a separated stem by about 1e-2 relative RMS.

local_patches.scope: ggml Vulkan cooperative-matrix attention backend only
local_patches.reason: An unaligned key count used to force shared-memory staging for every key block, with two workgroup barriers per QK contraction tile. Full F16/BF16 blocks may load directly; only the final partial block needs the existing guarded staging. Quantized decoding, partial head dimensions, attention context and accumulator precision are unchanged.

local_patches.scope: Intel Xe2 M8 cooperative attention with F16 K/V, H64 and F32 accumulation only
local_patches.reason: Preserve the native subgroup by default: matched B580 measurements found sixteen-lane subgroups slower despite fewer inactive output lanes. UTA_STUDIO_GGML_FA_SMALL_SUBGROUP explicitly tests SIMD16; the existing UTA_STUDIO_GGML_FA_SG32 override takes precedence and retains the native subgroup. UTA_STUDIO_GGML_FA_STAGE_KV tests full staging. Query/key context, F32 accumulators and other device/type paths are unchanged.

local_patches.scope: Cooperative attention query tiling; explicit larger-tile experiments only for Intel Xe2 F16 H64 F32-accumulator attention
local_patches.reason: Reuse each K matrix load across multiple sixteen-query tiles when explicitly requested. Keep the measured sixteen-query default: larger query tiles increase shared memory, cause register spills and regress B580 attention. UTA_STUDIO_GGML_FA_QUERY_ROWS accepts 16, 32 or 64 for recorded comparisons. Key context, masks, query layout and accumulator precision are unchanged. See docs/ROFORMER_B580_ATTENTION.md.

local_patches.scope: M8 F16 K/V H64 attention with F32 accumulation, sixteen query rows, thirty-two key columns and four SIMD32 subgroups
local_patches.reason: Reuse packed scores between row maximum and probability calculation, and reuse each V matrix operand across the two M8 query-row products. Per-output accumulation order, F16 probability rounding, F32 online state, full context, masks, tail handling and all barriers remain unchanged. Matched B580 XE90 model measurements reduce time attention from about 108.6 to 96.2 ms and frequency attention from 8.78 to 7.92 ms; both six-second output passes are byte-identical to the control. Every other shape/type retains the prior shader path. See docs/ROFORMER_B580_ATTENTION.md.

local_patches.scope: Intel Xe2 M8 F16 K/V H64 F32-accumulator attention with more than thirty-two queries, four native SIMD32 subgroups
local_patches.reason: Each subgroup owns eight complete query rows through QK, softmax and PV. Clustered four-lane row reductions, cached Q fragments, persistent F32 output fragments and coalesced shared K/V reduce the measured B580 time-attention kernel from 96.79 to 63.73 ms. The six-second production graph retains finite repeatable output with 72.05 dB SNR against the control; cross-version output is not bit-identical. Preserve full key context, existing F16 probability rounding, F32 accumulators, masks and tails. Small-query/GQA capacity and other device/type paths remain unchanged. UTA_STUDIO_GGML_FA_QUERY_OWNED=0 selects the prior path; explicit query-row or staging diagnostics also retain it. See docs/ROFORMER_B580_ATTENTION.md.

local_patches.scope: Existing Intel Xe2 native-SIMD32 H64 F16-K/V F32-accumulator query-owned attention only
local_patches.reason: Eight subgroups reuse one K/V tile while each still owns only eight query rows. Stream output through half-sized F32 scratch and load each rounded probability matrix once for four output contractions. Matched B580 XE90 model runs measure about 63.13 to 43.08 ms for time attention and 6.07 to 5.08 ms for frequency attention; complete six-second output WAVs are byte-identical. Full context, masks, tails, F32 state, accumulation order and the original small-query/GQA path remain unchanged. Retain four subgroups when device workgroup/shared-memory limits require it or UTA_STUDIO_GGML_FA_SHARED_GROUPS=4 explicitly requests the comparison. See docs/ROFORMER_B580_FRAGMENT_HANDOFF.md.

local_patches.scope: Intel Xe2 native-SIMD32 M8 H64 F32-accumulator query-owned attention with independent F16/F32 K/V storage
local_patches.reason: Load F32 or mixed K/V directly into the existing shared operand tile with the prior cooperative decoder's F16 rounding; no graph cast or global conversion tensor. Retain compact four/eight-subgroup workgroups, full context, masks, tails, accumulation order and other-device/type fallbacks. In six-second real graphs, Harmony time attention improves from 20.815 to 8.221 ms and Denoise from 20.663 to 8.139 ms; complete-output SNR is 67.04 and 74.42 dB, respectively, not bit-identical. Combined XE90 reaches 12.69 TFLOPS with bit-identical output against the seven-patch baseline. All 61 focused numerical fixtures pass. See docs/ROFORMER_B580_FLOATING_STORAGE.md.

local_patches.scope: Existing Intel Xe2 native-SIMD32 M8 H64 F32-accumulator query-owned attention with independent F16/F32 K/V storage
local_patches.reason: Publish eight independent F32 row scales per subgroup and use a zero-stride column-major cooperative load, replacing 128 scalar scale writes and one hot-loop score-overwrite barrier. Account for the extra 32 shared bytes per subgroup. Full context, F16 probability rounding, F32 state, accumulation order and device/type selection are unchanged. Recorded XE90-shape controls measure 43.916/43.010 ms versus 42.688/42.474 ms; three real model pairs retain byte-identical complete output, but do not establish a consistent whole-model speedup. All 61 default and 61 four-subgroup numerical fixtures pass. The padded score/probability experiment is rejected. See docs/ROFORMER_B580_COMPACT_RESCALE.md.
